reasoning: Both cable-1 and cable-2 Kelvin pairs are completely unrouted — all four nets /SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, /SENSEC2_HI, /SENSEC2_LO carry unconnected ratlines — making kelvin_pairs_gate_fail=2 per Rule 8, yet the scorer metric kelvin_unrouted=1. This 50% undercount means the optimizer receives only 1000 penalty units for a genuine two-cable Kelvin collapse. The directed stub summary exposes the root cause: zero /SENSEC* nets appear in the final stub list (only /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA), with absorbed=5. This satisfies the Rule 6 'absorber_kelvin_purge_detected' sentinel — all Kelvin stubs were consumed by the absorber before FR dispatch — and also meets Rule 7's abort condition (zero /SENSEC* in stub list, compile_failures empty, board has Kelvin pairs). Despite both abort conditions being met, FR was dispatched and returned a scored result; rule_enforcement_failures must be incremented. DRC=24 and 7 unconnected ratlines (of which 4 are Kelvin) confirm no quality gates pass. The primary fix needed is in the pipeline (absorber exclusion list), but a weight correction to the scorer is also warranted to give the optimizer a signal proportional to actual per-cable severity. Additionally, no existing rule requires that FR dispatch parameters be non-trivially changed between rounds for a persistently-failing cable — without such a requirement, the optimizer can cycle identical dispatches indefinitely for cable indices that the absorber is silently stranding.

scorer_penalty.rationale: kelvin_unrouted systematically undercounts failing cable pairs: it reports 1 when kelvin_pairs_gate_fail=2 (both cables completely failing, confirmed by all four /SENSEC{1,2}_HI/_LO nets present in failing_reasons). The existing weight of 1000 therefore applies 1000 penalty units where 2000 is warranted by actual cable-level severity. Raising to 2000 compensates for the ~50% undercount without requiring a metric-definition change, giving the optimizer a penalty signal proportional to the true number of failing Kelvin cable pairs. This raise is additive (increases a non-negative weight on an existing metric) and does not reward any bad metric.

manager_rule: When the same cable index N appears in kelvin_pairs_gate_fail in two or more consecutive rounds — i.e., any /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO net is present in failing_reasons for both round R and round R-1 — the manager MUST make at least one non-trivial, cable-specific change to the FR dispatch parameters before the next dispatch. Acceptable changes include: (a) adjusting the keepout or hint geometry specifically around cable N's Kelvin shunt window, (b) changing the directed stub endpoint, width, or layer assignment for /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO, or (c) modifying opt_time or seed in a way that is demonstrably different from the prior round's value AND accompanied by a geometric hint change for cable N. A change is non-trivial only if it could plausibly alter cable N's local routing topology; changing a global seed without altering the stub geometry for cable N does not qualify. If the manager cannot identify any non-trivial change for a cable that has failed in two consecutive rounds, that cable constitutes a confirmed local minimum: the manager must immediately escalate to human review, providing (a) the cable index, (b) the specific nets failing, (c) the FR dispatch parameters used in each failing round, and (d) the stub geometry (endpoints, net, width, layer) for the failing cable in each round. FR must not be dispatched again for a persistently-failing cable whose stub and hint parameters are identical to those of the prior failing round.
